item.title: The Euler Characteristic of Spherical Bestvina-Brady Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.19203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the Euler characteristic of Bestvina-Brady kernels $\operatorname{BB}(\Gamma)$ for all Artin groups of spherical type. Our method involves discrete Morse theory to describe the cellular structure of a classifying space for the Bestvina--Brady kernel, through the action of $\operatorname{BB}(\Gamma)$ on non-integer level sets of the universal cover of the Salvetti complex. We extend the method of computation of $\chi(\operatorname{BB}(\Gamma))$ to Artin groups that satisfy the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture and whose nerves are rationally acyclic, and we provide an example by realising the projective plane as the nerve of a Coxeter group.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Flores Mart\'inez

item.title: An analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible classes and radicality for finite irreducible Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.19251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, $M$ a $G$-module, and $F$ a field. A continuous group homomorphism $i : \Gamma_L=\text{Gal}(L_{\text{sep}}/L) \rightarrow G$ yields a homomorphism $i^* : H^d(G,M) \rightarrow H^d(L,M)$ for every $d\in \mathbb{N}$. An element $u \in H^d(G,M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $u\in\ker(i^*)$ for every $i$ and every field extension $L/F$. If $M=\mathbb{F}_p$ for a prime $p$ with a trivial $G$-action, an element $u$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if $u^k$ is negligible over $F$ for some $k\geq1$. The (eventually) negligible elements over $F$ form an ideal of the cohomology ring $H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$, called the (eventually) negligible ideal. We prove an analog of Quillen-Venkov for eventually negligible elements. An element $u\in H^*(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is eventually negligible over $F$ if and only if the restriction of $u$ to the cohomology of each elementary abelian $p$-subgroup of $G$ is eventually negligible over $F$. Paired with applications of a Gysin-type long exact sequence, we identify generators of the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of dihedral groups, cyclic $2$-groups, and generalized quaternion groups. We prove that the negligible ideal over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the mod-2 cohomology of every finite irreducible Coxeter group is radical. The result was previously known for Weyl groups; we prove it for the remaining non-Weyl types $I_2(m)$, $H_3$, and $H_4$.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Cedillo Vayson de Pradenne, Matthew Gherman, Enoch Guo, Colin La

item.title: Conformal dimension and self-similar groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.19260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Ahlfors-regular conformal dimension of spaces with locally expanding self-covering maps and, more generally, limit spaces of contracting self-similar groups. We show that the conformal dimension is characterized by combinatorial moduli associated with the Schreier graphs of these groups. We compare these moduli with contraction coefficients of self-similar group actions and with algebras of functions on the limit spaces satisfying asymptotic $p$-energy conditions. We also give conditions on the group when the conformal dimension is equal to the infimum of visual metrics on the self-similarity complex.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Nekrashevych

item.title: Invariable Generation of Groups of Homeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.19666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a sufficient condition for a group of homeomorphisms of a compact Hausdorff space to be non-invariably generated, generalizing previous results proved using the dynamics of a group's action. We exhibit new applications among Scott-R\"over-Nekrashevych groups and among groups of tree automorphism of with (almost) locally prescribed actions.
item.dc:creator: Neelam, Davide Perego, Matteo Tarocchi

item.title: Prefixes of Coxeter elements are Coxeter elements of the reflection subgroups they generate
item.description: arXiv:2610.19755v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(W,S)$ be a Coxeter system of finite rank, let $T$ be its set of reflections and let $c \in W$ be a Coxeter element. For $x$ in the interval $[1,c]_T$ of the absolute order, let $P(x)$ be the subgroup generated by the reflections $t\le_T x$. We prove that $x$ is a Coxeter element of $P(x)$ with respect to the canonical Coxeter generators of $P(x)$, that $P(x)$ is generated by the factors of any reduced reflection factorization of $x$, and that the Hurwitz action on the reduced reflection factorizations of $x$ is transitive. The proof reduces the general case to the case of a Coxeter system whose Coxeter matrix has entries in $\{1,2,3,\infty\}$, which was treated by Hubery and Krause.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Wegener

item.title: Maximal subgroups of topological full groups of shifts of finite type
item.description: arXiv:2610.20024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study maximal subgroups of topological full groups of irreducible one-sided shifts of finite type whose associated groupoids have Cantor unit space. For each wide open subgroupoid of such a groupoid, we construct a subgroupoid graph and identify the subgroupoid with a full compact open reduction of the corresponding countable graph groupoid. Every minimal wide open subgroupoid is either AF or purely infinite. A proper wide open subgroupoid is prime if it admits no proper intermediate wide open subgroupoid. We prove a trichotomy for prime subgroupoids: they are minimal, arise from a clopen bipartition, or have a unique nonempty proper closed invariant set, which is nowhere dense. For a prime subgroupoid, the normalizer of its topological full group is maximal in the ambient topological full group precisely when it maps onto the ambient abelianization. An analogous criterion holds in every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup. For a minimal prime subgroupoid, its topological full group is maximal precisely when it equals its normalizer and the inclusion induces a surjection on first groupoid homology. We also describe all fully amplified maximal subgroups, namely those closed under local agreement. For Thompson's group $V$, the stabilizer of every simple type system is maximal, extending results of Belk, Bleak, Quick and Skipper for finite type systems and certain classes of infinite ones. Finally, every subgroup containing the ambient commutator subgroup has continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic maximal subgroups acting minimally on the unit space.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui

item.title: On the maximum relational complexity of affine groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.20077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a group of permutations of a set $\Omega$. The relational complexity $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is the least integer $r\geq 2$ such that the $G$-orbit of every finite tuple is determined by the $G$-orbits of its $r$-subtuples; there is currently only a small collection of groups $G$ for which $\mathrm{RC}(G)$ is known precisely. In this paper we study the relational complexity of finite affine groups acting naturally on a $d$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that every such group has relational complexity at most $d+2$ when $q>2$ and at most $d+1$ when $q=2$; we produce a complete classification of the primitive such groups for which these bounds are attained.
item.dc:creator: Coen del Valle, Nick Gill, Pablo Spiga

item.title: The finite basis problem and subvariety intervals for max-plus matrix semirings
item.description: arXiv:2610.20257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S=(\N,\max,+)$ be the max-plus algebra of the nonnegative integers, and let $\overline S$ be obtained from $S$ by adjoining $-\infty$ as a semiring zero. We first prove that the varieties generated by the full matrix semirings $\Mat_n(S)$ and by the upper triangular matrix semirings $\UT_n(\overline S)$ form strictly ascending chains. Every interval between distinct members of either chain has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$ and contains a chain and an antichain of that cardinality. The proof uses finite syntactic semirings associated with prime-cycle languages and an independent family of identities. We then construct finite commutative ai-semirings from languages of monomials closed under divisibility and prove their bounded-variable property by cancellation, explicit integer evaluations and independence in a free abelian group. A loop-block identity for upper triangular matrices and dimension-independent cubic-padding identities for full matrices show that every variety in each of the above intervals has infinite axiomatic rank. In fact, every variety between $\V(S)$ and the variety generated by all full matrix dimensions has infinite axiomatic rank. These varieties are therefore nonfinitely based, also relative to the ai-semiring axioms. Finally, for every fixed full matrix dimension, we prove equational equivalence over all six positive or nonnegative integer, rational and real coefficient domains. The original convex-ideal countermodels and their full-matrix transfer proof are recalled separately for comparison; they are not used in the algebraic proofs. Throughout, the signature consists of two binary operations and contains no constant symbols.
item.dc:creator: Jun Jiao, Mengya Yue

item.title: Equational theories of flat semirings $S(W)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the finite basis problem for flat semirings of the form $S(W)$, where $W$ is a nonempty set of nonempty words, possibly infinite. We prove that $S(W)$ is finitely based if and only if the strict interior of every word in $W$ is linear; here the strict interior of a word is obtained by deleting its first and last letters. This completely resolves an open problem raised by Jackson et al.~(J. Algebra 611: 211--245, 2022).
item.dc:creator: Zidong Gao, Yilin Zhou

item.title: Generation by lazy and invertible cellular automata over the Klein four-group
item.description: arXiv:2610.20329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G=C_2\times C_2$ and $A=\{0,1\}$. We characterize the submonoid of $\text{CA}(G;A)$ generated by lazy and invertible cellular automata. A cellular automaton belongs to this submonoid if and only if, whenever it maps the two free $G$-orbits onto the same free orbit, it maps both constant configurations and some two-point orbit to the same constant. The proof gives a factorization using elementary orbit collapses and three two-cell lazy maps. The criterion yields the cardinality $59\,712$ and identifies the maps missed by a weaker constant-separation invariant. Adjoining one idempotent generates the full monoid, and the generated submonoid is contained in exactly one maximal proper submonoid, of cardinality $65\,024$. The submonoid generated by lazy maps alone has $4\,007$ elements, and for both generating sets the maximum shortest-word length is six. The criterion and the cardinalities $59\,712$ and $4\,007$ are formally verified in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Alcal\'{a}-Arroyo, Alonso Castillo-Ramirez, Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang

item.title: Motion groups, Legendrian links, and non-trivial loops of embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.10804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce, for an embedded Legendrian link~$L$ in a contact 3-manifold~$(M,\xi)$, the group of its \emph{Legendrian motions}. Analogously with the smooth case, we prove that this Legendrian motion group is isomorphic to the fundamental group of the space of unparametrised Legendrian embeddings. For all Legendrian knots in the standard contact 3-sphere, we characterise Legendrian motions in terms of contact mapping classes of the knot exterior. In an appendix, we give a short exposition of our techniques applied to the smooth case, comparing to the classical Dahm homomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Corrigan, Isacco Nonino

item.title: Invariant factors from products of cyclotomic polynomials, with applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.19205v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f,g\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be products of cyclotomic polynomials such that either $g/\gcd(f,g)$ or $f/\gcd(f,g)$ (or both) is squarefree. We give explicit formulae for the invariant factors of $f(C_g)$, where $C_g$ is the companion matrix of $g$, expressing them in terms of the indices and multiplicities of the cyclotomic factors of $f$ and $g$. A more compact formula holds for the circulant case $g(t)=t^n-1$, assuming that every cyclotomic factor shared by $f$ and $g$ has multiplicity $1$ in $f$. We discuss applications to several topics, including abelianizations of cyclically presented groups, homology groups of cyclic branched covers of knots, adjacency matrices and shifted graph Laplacians, $K$-theory, and Smith forms of matrix powers. For example, for two families of hyperbolic knots we give the first integral homology in every covering degree; or, when $g$ is squarefree, we determine the least eventual period of the Smith forms of powers of $f(C_g)$.
item.dc:creator: Vanni Noferini, Gerald Williams

item.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19787v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara, Ryokichi Tanaka

item.title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $\alpha$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.
item.dc:creator: Kewei Li

item.title: The zero divisor and augmentation conjectures for medial quandle rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.20306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For quandle rings, Bardakov--Passi--Singh and Elhamdadi--Nunez--Singh respectively formulated an analogue of Kaplansky's zero divisor conjecture and a weakened analogue of Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture involving the augmentation map. In this note, we verify these conjectures for medial quandles. The latter holds for a larger class of quandles; we characterize integral domains over which the statement holds for this class. We also characterize integral domains of characteristic 0 over which the statement holds for a given finite Alexander quandle.
item.dc:creator: Luc Ta

item.title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.20478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $\Gamma_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ \Gamma_n(M)/K_n(M)\cong\pi_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Ocampo

item.title: Universally extendible characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.20520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let theta be an ordinary character or a Brauer character of a finite group N. We show that theta extends to every overgroup $G=G_\theta\trianglerighteq N$ if and only if Z(N) <= Ker(theta) and the deflated character of Inn(N) extends to Aut(N)_theta. This equivalence is compatible with fields of values. A similar investigation for extensions from subnormal subgroups leads to a new characteristic subgroup of N.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Sambale

item.title: Compressed primitivity problem in free groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.21499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a fixed integer $r\ge 2$, we prove that the \emph{compressed primitivity problem} in the free group $F_r=F(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ is decidable in non-deterministic polynomial time. That is, for a \emph{straight-line program} $\mathcal A$ over $\{x_1,\dots,x_r\}^{\pm1}$ representing an element $g\in F_r$, the problem of deciding whether $g$ is primitive in $F_r$ belongs to $\mathsf{NP}$, with input measured by the size of $\mathcal A$. For $r=2$, we prove that this problem is decidable in deterministic polynomial time. We also show that, in every fixed rank $r\ge 2$, automorphic minimality of the conjugacy class of a compressed word in $F_r$ is decidable in deterministic polynomial time.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Kapovich

item.title: Property $(T)$ and nonlinearity of mapping class group quotients
item.description: arXiv:2609.12196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a general method for proving Kazhdan's property $(T)$ for quotients $G/K_{[c+1]}$, where $G$ is countable, $K$ is a normal subgroup and $K_{[j]}$ denotes its lower central series. The method combines an affine realization of $G/[K,K]$, a contraction argument, and permanence for nilpotent normal subgroups. We apply this method to several classes of groups by means of homological representations. For the Torelli lower-central series quotients $\operatorname{Mod}(\Sigma_g)/(\mathcal{T}_g)_{[c+1]}$ for $g\ge3$ we show that they have property $(T)$ for every $c\ge1$. We also prove property $(T)$ for $\operatorname{Aut}(F_3)/(\mathrm{IA}_3)_{[c+1]}$ for every $c\ge1$, relating these groups to the tame nilpotent images studied by Lubotzky and Pak. Several other classes of examples are discussed as well. We also prove that the Torelli lower-central series quotients for $c\ge2$ are not residually finite, and thus non-linear.
item.dc:creator: Piotr W. Nowak

item.title: Classes of Subgroups of a finite group with isomorphic quotient groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.13076v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the poset QIso(G) of classes of subgroups of a finite group G having isomorphic quotients. Particularly, we study it for finite abelian groups and for some classes of non-abelian metacyclic groups, namely dihedral groups Dn, the group U2np and affine groups Aff(F) over finite field F. In the case of abelian groups G, we show that there exists a duality from QIso(G) to Iso(G). We show that cyclic groups are the only groups for which QIso(G), up to duality is isomorphic to its subgroup lattice. We also show that cyclic groups are the only nilpotent groups for which QIso(G), up to duality is isomorphic to its lattice of normal subgroups. We characterize finite 2-groups all of whose subgroups are q-self dual with QIso(G) being a chain. We also characterize all p-groups G of order at most p4 whose QIso(G) is a chain.
item.dc:creator: Tushar Halder, Sachin Ballal

item.title: On identities in connected topological groups
item.description: arXiv:2406.05203v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a connected (indeed, path-connected) Hausdorff topological group G such that, for an odd n >= 665, the identity x^n = e holds in some neighbourhood of the identity but does not hold in the whole group. This answers in the negative a question of Mycielski and Aronszajn (Question 2.48 of the Kourovka Notebook). The construction uses the Graev extension of metrics to free topological groups and results of Adian and Adian-Atabekyan (for n > 10^10, alternatively, of Ol'shanskii and Ashmanov-Ol'shanskii) on free Burnside groups and their central extensions.
item.dc:creator: I. N. Zyabrev, E. A. Reznichenko
